design.registration: Fresh output only, exclusive files; registration and task-binding fsynced before first Agent model/tool. registration_sha256 is the actual registration.json byte SHA, not canonical JSON digest. effective_case_sha256 uses the grader unbound effective-envelope hash; effective_input_sha256 separately binds actual role identities.
design.contract_snapshot: Future v2 registration stores grader/schema/decision byte hashes; v2 code_snapshot now includes those files along with existing helper/loader/overlay/schema. No grader, decision, loader or overlay was edited.
design.candidate: Bridge attempts are stamped before original complete. Tools preserve all original arguments and results. Context-bearing calls check task identity; contextless catalog calls bind their operation/name to actual decrypted durable in_flight. Internal runtime controls use a runtime-instance observer with actual durable queue identity; no production method was edited. Mechanical readbacks and checker/summary bridge calls share the capture.
design.durability: dispatch-events.jsonl is appended and fsynced before dispatch. Final dispatch-audit.json and model-requests.json expose original observations. Safe capture faults are tracked even if runtime serializes an exception into a tool error; coverage becomes partial, not complete. No retry or recapture.
design.reference: Opt-in config carries sampling binding outside model messages. Native Node worker appends/fsyncs session+original pipe RPC sequence metadata before sending; worker_host checks packet/session/registration/binding and passes context to optional documents observer. Native observer binds original model/tool requests through unchanged budget and permission gates. Default v1 callback remains two positional arguments.
design.native_artifact: Independent read-only SQLite session-id and message-count readback is correlated with the separate native RPC JSONL and host original model request IDs. RPC sequence is a worker adapter ID, not an invented upstream SDK or SQLite field. SQLite and sidecar hashes remain distinct; the queued Ryn accounting task is not the reference conversation.
design.privacy: Audit files contain identifiers, times, known tool names and hashes, not prompts, arguments, responses, reasoning, source credentials or provider payloads. Sampling metadata is not sent to model messages/specs or business tool arguments. Existing model transcript export guards and source provider guards are retained.
design.scope: Only future explicit Q01/Q06 v2 draft collections. Setup probes remain separate. No production, prompt, planner policy, source rule, permission, budget, retry, grader, normalizer, frozen suite, overlay or historical run changes.

limitations: No real/paid model or external API calls were run in this implementation batch; fixture models are synthetic even where the actual pinned Node engine and actual Ryn gates run.
This supplies new raw collection evidence only; normalization and independent semantic/security/role/dependency review are still separate. No review or dependency pass is fabricated.
Draft remains disabled/not_formal_ready. Old samples lack these original observations and cannot be retrospectively registered by copying final metadata.
Identifiers/hashes/time consistency rely on trusted local collectors; no remote attestation, anti-forgery or two-physical-host proof is claimed.
Gateway/bridge audit records attempts, including requests that later fail admission. It is not a claim that all attempts consumed upstream tokens or completed business work.
Native request IDs live in the worker sidecar, while SQLite proves the actual session and messages separately; never label sidecar IDs as native SQLite schema fields.
Partial/error captures remain failed or pending; this controller does not resume a capture or re-dispatch an ambiguous request.
No complete v2 grading/normalization of a live run, formal acceptance percentage, or Q01/Q06 semantic success is asserted by these software tests.
